name: Micro-Conversion Step Drop-Off Audit
phase: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that [Step 3 in our onboarding flow] causes unnecessary user drop-off. We will verify this by instrumenting telemetry across every form field and screen transition, and consider it validated if simplifying that single step reduces drop-off by ≥ 30% without lowering downstream activation quality.
schematic: Read at step 3 of the 3-step strip

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Map every input field, click and screen transition in the target path into one sequential funnel.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Log drop-off, validation errors and interaction time for every field across 500 sessions.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Plot the drop-off gradient across each micro-step to find the friction points.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Map every user input field, click, and screen transition in the target path into a sequential funnel model.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Log drop-off percentages, validation errors, and interaction times for every field across 500 user sessions.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Plot the drop-off gradient across each micro-step to identify points of user friction.

warning.label: Removing Essential Friction
warning.text: Cutting identity checks or qualification questions lifts completion and floods you with spam.

warningFull: Streamlining onboarding forms by cutting out identity checks or qualification questions can boost completion rates while flooding the product with unqualified or spam accounts.
